A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RNA proof-reading is controlled by the coordination of RNA and nucleotide binding to the RIG-I protein, with implications for autoimmune disease, cancer, and the design of RNA-targeting therapeutics.
the selectivity filter for RIG-I is a conserved motif that couples RNA and ATP binding and that this motif is critical for the function of RIG-I.
we show that RIG-I uses RNA proof-reading as a mechanism to selectively recognize viral RNA, and we show that RNA proof-reading is controlled by coordination with ATP binding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RNA and ATP binding can be coordinated to regulate RNA binding selectivity.
the ATP-gated mechanism for RNA proof-reading is an evolutionarily conserved feature of the RIG-I protein that is essential for its function.
RNA proof-reading in RIG-I is a dynamic, regulated, process, and not a passive, static, process.
